description:
FILED s464ax from the #982 key-text probe (48 numeric values, printed AND used
as hash keys, vs perl 5.40.3).  PRE-EXISTING â reproduces on main `80b715c`
and on `0e54656`; it is the ONE row of that battery that differs.

    my $a = 1e15;               print "$a\n";   # perl 1e+15   PCL 1000000000000000
    my $c = 1000000000000000.0; print "$c\n";   # perl 1e+15   PCL 1000000000000000
    my $d = 1e15 + 0.5;         print "$d\n";   # perl 1e+15   PCL 1000000000000000
    my $e = 1e16;               print "$e\n";   # perl 1e+16   PCL 1e+16     (agree)
    my $f = 1e14;               print "$f\n";   # perl 1e+14?  no: both 100000000000000

So the divergence is exactly at |v| = 1e15, i.e. at the %.15g switch point.

WHERE.  `stringify-value`'s float arm in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:

    (exp10 (floor (log abs-v (coerce 10 (type-of v)))))
    (if (and (>= exp10 -4) (< exp10 15)) <fixed> <exponential>)

`(log 1e15 10.0d0)` in double float is 14.999999999999998, so FLOOR gives 14,
the test `(< 14 15)` is true, and the fixed branch prints all 16 digits.
perl's Gconvert switches to exponential when the decimal exponent reaches the
precision (15), which 1e15 does.

FIX SHAPE: do not derive the exponent from a LOG.  Either compare against the
exact decimal thresholds (`(>= abs-v 1d15)` / `(< abs-v 1d-4)`), or compute
the exponent from the printed form.  The threshold comparison is exact in
double float because 1d15 is representable.  Probe the neighbours after
fixing: 999999999999999.9, 1e15-1, 1e15, 1e15+1, 1e-4, 9.999e-5.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: `1e14 * 10` prints as the integer text in perl too
(perl's own IV/NV bookkeeping), and PCL agrees there â so do not "fix" that
one into exponential.  The rule is about the VALUE's magnitude on the NV
path, not about how it was computed.

SIZE: small, one arm.  No baseline row is known to sit behind it (found by
probe).  A filler.  Coordinate with whoever owns `stringify-value` at the
time â s464aw was working on the overload/conversion arms of the same
function in the same round.

=== DONE (s473d) ===
SHIPPED as member 4 of s473d, commit "member 4 (#1012): `%.15g`'s style switch
is the exponent of the ROUNDED value -- and a log cannot compute it".

THE RULE (now docs/ir-spec.md section 3.2, normative): C uses the exponential
style when the decimal exponent of the value AFTER ROUNDING TO 15 SIGNIFICANT
DIGITS is < -4 or >= 15.  PCL read that exponent off a logarithm and never
applied the rounding, and both halves were wrong:

  * (log 1d15 10.0d0) is 14.999999999999998, so FLOOR gave 14 and every exact
    power of ten from 1e15 up printed its digits;
  * the rounding is the rule: 999999999999999.9 rounds up to 1e15 and perl
    prints 1e+15, while 999999999999999.0 prints its own digits, and
    9.999999999999999e-5 rounds up to 1e-4 and prints 0.0001.

%p-decimal-exponent corrects the log against exact rational powers of ten (each
loop runs at most once) and applies the rounding.  Fixing the branch EXPOSED a
latent bug whose own comment was the false claim: SBCL's ~,14E does NOT
renormalise a mantissa that rounds up to 10 (it gave 10.00000000000000d+14 ->
"10e+14"), so %p-exponential-15 builds the mantissa by rounding in RATIONALS
against the already-computed exponent.

THE SIBLING SITE IS THE SAME READING (rule 11): sprintf-format-float-g
corrected its log for the mantissa RANGE but not for the rounding CARRY, so
`sprintf "%g", 999999.9` printed 1000000 where perl prints 1e+06.  It now calls
%p-decimal-exponent with its own precision -- one function for both.

RESIDUE, named and asserted rather than left as a surprise: perl holds an
integral ARITHMETIC result as an IV and prints its digits, while the same value
written as a float literal is an NV -- `1e14*10` is 1000000000000000 and `1e15`
is 1e+15.  PCL has one representation for both.  Task #1369, with the measured
12-shape table (8 agree / 4 diverge BEFORE and AFTER: the fix MOVES the
divergence and makes it uniform, it does not create it);
docs/not-supported.md section "Integers are unbounded" gained it as a fourth
face; Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t D2 asserts it.

BARS: runtime-only, so NO generation bump (corpus-diff emission IDENTICAL over
111 files + 6 shapes, silent drops 5 unchanged).  Two probe files (a 50-value
spelling table and the 12 routes to 1e15) byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 apart
from the named residue, under the default emission AND PCL_OPT=none.  Gate 223
files / 7705 rows, xs-only.  Guard Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t D1+D2,
inverse-verified FAILING on a c4304834 extraction.  Final tree: sweep TOTAL
18674 (+0) GATE clean; companion op/ leg 0 movers.
subject: A float whose magnitude is exactly 1e15 stringifies as its integer text; perl says 1e+15
